items.text: The guests remain in turmoil as the believers and skeptics argue among one another.
Fear and confusion quickly spread through them, like ink in water, and soon ...

items.speaker: Trial Taker I
items.text: Haha! I did it! I put on the mask!

items.speaker: Trial Taker II
items.text: I-I'm saved!

items.speaker: Trial Taker II
items.text: Thank you, thank you, Ms. Grace!

items.speaker: Forsaken I
items.text: It hurts! It hurts so much.

items.speaker: Forsaken II
items.text: Help ... *roar*

items.speaker: Sonetto
items.text: We can't let more of these people give in to their fears!
Her voice is almost entirely drowned out by the roaring crowd.

items.speaker: Kamuta
items.text: These stubborn outsiders must be silenced! Take them away!

items.speaker: Kamuta
items.text: Let our revenge begin with them!

items.speaker: Toa
items.text: For Nukutaeao!

items.speaker: Kamuta
items.text: Selone, take my troubled sister back to her room. The softness of her heart has clouded her judgment, just as her shell shows.

items.speaker: Selone
items.text: Chief ...
Black ink seems to stain every one of their faces.
The upheaval has engulfed the Nukutai along with countless other innocents.

items.speaker: Child
items.text: Mum, I wanna go home.

items.speaker: Grieving Mother
items.text: Just think of something happy, sweetheart.

items.speaker: Grieving Mother
items.text: Remember that toy your dad bought you? It's waiting for you at home. We'll be there soon. Just put this on. We'll be there soon.
Trembling, the mother slowly lowers the mask to her child's face.

items.speaker: Barcarola
items.text: No!
Barcarola lunges forward, knocking the Manus mask out of her hand.

items.speaker: Ms. Grace
items.text: I don't believe your job description permits you to interrupt our guests, does it, Ms. Barcarola?

items.speaker: Barcarola
items.text: I don't understand, Captain Grace. Why are you letting this happen? Why are you doing this?
Grace carefully picks up the still-humming mask and brushes off the dust. She steps forward.

items.speaker: Ms. Grace
items.text: Cheer up, dear girl. Hold that chin up high. Now that's the spirit, the brightest star of the "Free Breeze" forever and always.

items.speaker: Ms. Grace
items.text: Just take a look. Your loyal fans are waiting for your next show.

items.speaker: Ms. Grace
items.text: Won't you play some of those beautiful melodies for them again?

items.speaker: Barcarola
items.text: But Ms. Grace, what do you mean by the "Storm" and diseases of the world, and this new era?

items.speaker: Ms. Grace
items.text: Oh, it's all so much simpler than you think, Ms. Barcarola.

items.speaker: Ms. Grace
items.text: In the new era, all that you hated in this time will vanish, as if it had never been there at all.

items.speaker: Ms. Grace
items.text: The "City of Violins" you swore you'd never return to will soon be forgotten, washed away in the coming "Storm."

items.speaker: Ms. Grace
items.text: Your wish will come true. You'll never need return to it. You couldn't even if you tried.

items.speaker: Barcarola
items.text: Never again?
Memories of her home return to her as if she were there just yesterday.
The towering bell tower of the cathedral, the creaking footbridges of the dock, the Cremona Music Festival competitor list that never displayed her name, and the distant scent of torta and risotto.
She has been far away from that world for so long, yet there before her eyes, she sees it again: the report card scribbled with red ink soaring on the wind.

items.speaker: Ms. Grace
items.text: What was it you said about that rotten little town? The monotony of sound, the disappointment of those old fossils and their little worlds—is that right?

items.speaker: Barcarola
items.text: Yes. I said I never, never wanted to go back.

items.speaker: Ms. Grace
items.text: Now, keep your hand steady this time, my dear. You must be certain.
Cold metal meets Barcarola's hand, jolting her back to reality.
Her trembling hand reaches for her peculiar, silent instrument. She cradles it in her arms.

items.speaker: Barcarola
items.text: My Crackling Box.
The familiar texture of the adhesive holding it together reassures her. She runs her fingers over it before greedily moving on to the rest.
Then, in the intricate structure of the instrument she created, she finds all the pieces of that familiar thing.
A fingerboard, strings, a sound post, a bridge, tuning pegs ...
A violin.

items.speaker: Barcarola
items.text: No!
A sudden warmth bursts forth within her, urging her to push the mask aside.
